title: Transport Mechanisms
standard_text: Transport mechanisms: the fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane; passive transport (diffusion, facilitated diffusion, osmosis); active transport; endocytosis and exocytosis; surface area to volume ratio. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Biology 1, Quarter 1)
meta_desc: Free Biology 1 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 1): the cell membrane, diffusion, osmosis, active transport, bulk transport and surface area to volume ratio. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Passive transport needs no energy; active transport needs ATP.
key_sub: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a membrane.
body_html:
How to think about it

The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins (fluid mosaic model). Small molecules such as oxygen diffuse from high to low concentration; water moves by osmosis through the partially permeable membrane; ions and glucose cross with the help of channel and carrier proteins (facilitated diffusion).

Active transport uses ATP and carrier proteins to move substances against a concentration gradient, as in root hair cells taking in minerals. Large particles enter by endocytosis and leave by exocytosis. Small cells have a large surface area to volume ratio, so exchange is efficient.

Example

A red blood cell is put in pure water. What happens?

Water moves in

Answer: it swells and may burst

Example

Cube of side 2 cm: surface area to volume ratio?

24 ÷ 8

Answer: 3 : 1

Common mistakes

  • Thinking osmosis moves solutes.
  • Thinking diffusion needs energy.
  • Mixing up hypotonic and hypertonic.
